label: Power bank or charger

questions.why: Power banks and wall chargers need different care.

questions.text: Is it used or left in hot places, such as a car or in the sun?
What cable is used with it?
questions.why: Damaged or poor cables can overheat.

answers.label: The one it came with or a branded one

questions.why: A hard drop can damage the battery inside a power bank.

questions.text: Is it charged under pillows or on beds?
Have you noticed swelling, very high heat, a smell or sparks?
questions.why: Early signs let you get it checked before a small fault grows.

care_tips.text: Stop using the power bank and keep it away from anything that can burn if the battery swells, gets very hot or smells unusual.
care_tips.why: A damaged battery can catch fire.

care_tips.text: Don't open, puncture or crush the battery, and don't use it after a hard fall that dented it.
care_tips.why: Damaged battery cells can overheat or catch fire.

care_tips.text: Unplug the charger from the wall before cleaning it, and don't use it if it is damaged or wet.
care_tips.why: A damaged or wet charger can give a shock.

care_tips.text: Use a branded cable in good condition.
Charge on a hard, cool surface, not under pillows or on beds.
Keep it out of hot cars and direct sun.
After a hard drop, watch the power bank for heat or swelling and stop using it if either appears.
care_tips.why: Inner damage can show up later.

reminders.text: Check the power bank and cables for damage, swelling or heat.
reminders.note: Check your manual for the interval for your model.
